page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-112 is an x86_64 server instance powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors, providing 112 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 56 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 896 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. This configuration includes no integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote network-attached block storage for persistent data requirements.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier multi-threaded compute capability, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 164,204.56 and a PassMark CPU score of 94,622.94, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. Synthetic memory throughput tests reflect high read-only cached bandwidth of 7,672.69 GB/sec alongside solid large-block uncached read speeds of 274.66 GB/sec. Highly parallel workloads such as Clang compilation (54,854.0) and ray tracing (105,673.0) demonstrate strong scaling. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,648.0 and gzip compression of 28.09 GB/sec, fall into mid-tier performance bands.

From a resource utilization standpoint, the high thread density paired with 896 GB of RAM enables substantial resource consolidation for memory-heavy parallel tasks without unneeded GPU costs. A technical tradeoff is the absence of AVX-512 instruction support, which, alongside the lack of discrete GPUs, results in lower generation speeds for large language model workloads. The instance is well matched for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, intensive multi-threaded compilation pipelines, and high-concurrency enterprise applications.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-112 is a high-density instance configured with 112 dedicated vCPUs from AMD EPYC 7B13 processors across 56 physical cores and 896 GB of system RAM. Delivering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, it excludes local storage and discrete GPUs, relying entirely on networked storage. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput, securing top-decile ranks in PassMark CPU tests (94,622.94) and multi-core stress testing (164,204.56), complemented by robust cached memory bandwidth exceeding 7.6 TB/sec. Single-threaded metrics reflect median levels. Due to the lack of AVX-512 extensions and dedicated accelerators, the instance exhibits poor throughput on large-model machine learning generation. Instead, its high thread count and large memory footprint provide an efficient balance for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, large in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-throughput static web serving, and expansive software build pipelines.
